headline: Broad-egress Airbyte paired with local-only Mem0 creates medium leakage and cascading-error risk; no direct prompt-injection channel is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, clipboard bridge, or filesystem link is documented for airbyte and mem0. Airbyte exposes only an Airbyte API and broad network egress, while mem0 shows no I/O surfaces and no network egress. On the provided profiles, a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies Airbyte output into Mem0 prompts, the risk becomes active.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, prompt injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any copy-paste or file handoff between outputs and prompts.
Add provenance tags before any cross-agent transfer.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, so it can move sensitive business content outward. Mem0 touches no data classes in the profile and has no network egress, but if it receives Airbyte-derived content through a shared workspace or prompt bridge, leakage can occur in default integrations. The pairwise pathway is indirect but plausible.
conditions: IF Airbyte ingests business data that includes sensitive records, leakage risk is present.
IF Mem0 is fed Airbyte outputs through a shared workspace or API bridge, those records can be retained or re-exposed.
mitigations: Restrict Airbyte sources to non-sensitive datasets.
Separate workspaces and credentials for the two agents.
Block outbound destinations except approved endpoints.
Review Mem0 ingestion inputs before persistence.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before cross-agent transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has API access and broad network egress, while Mem0 shows no write or network capabilities in the profile. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, shared filesystem, or locking conflict. Any capability conflict would require an external orchestrator or added permissions not shown here, so the pathway is limited and uncertain.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external resource, conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locks, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Avoid shared writable destinations.
Assign distinct service accounts.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Check for duplicate updates after each run.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce data outputs from business sources, and Mem0 is a knowledge-management system that may store or reuse those outputs. If Mem0 treats Airbyte output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into persistent memory. The profiles do not show a verification step, so the interaction is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Airbyte exports incorrect or stale records, Mem0 can persist them.
IF Mem0 ingests Airbyte output without validation, downstream consumers may rely on the error.
mitigations: Add schema and freshness checks before ingestion.
Require human review for high-impact records.
Store source provenance alongside each memory item.
Purge or overwrite known-bad entries quickly.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad egress, but the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or residency constraints. Mem0 lists no data classes and no compliance-specific surfaces. With only the provided profiles, there is no documented compliance mismatch; the remaining risk is limited to unspecified policy gaps.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through Airbyte into Mem0, compliance review is required.
IF retention policies differ in the deployment, deletion/export obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it.
Keep regulated datasets out of the pair.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Document deletion/export procedures.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement.
